rooms.heading:
A room for
{{one subject.}}
body: Twelve is only a number until you know what kind of rooms they are. The distinction that matters is **specialised against general**: a chemistry laboratory with gas taps, a fume path and reagent shelves is a different object from a science room with a sink at the back — and only one of them lets a class run a practical the board expects.

Physics, Chemistry and Biology each carry **board practicals from Class IX to Class XII**. The mathematics laboratory is the one most schools do without: its purpose is to make mathematics something handled rather than only argued on paper.

body: The school enumerates its twelve rooms by name, and **four of the twelve are inquiry rooms rather than subject laboratories** — counted inside the twelve, not added to it. A school that spends four of twelve on debate, making, maps and open-ended work has chosen to give space to the subjects that do not sit an exam.

The Robotics Lab is set out on [STEM, Robotics & Enrichment](/academics/teaching-learning/stem-robotics/); the language laboratory on [Reading, Language & Library](/academics/teaching-learning/reading-language/).

spaces.heading:
Rooms for the work
{{with no right answer.}}
body: Great learning does not come from memorising. It comes from asking, trying, failing safely and trying again — which needs rooms built for experimentation, discussion, making and practical work rather than for listening.

cells.label: Science laboratories
cells.value: Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics — practical spaces, not a science room with a sink.

cells.label: Language lab
cells.value: Spoken language, practised aloud, recorded and reviewed.

cells.label: Academic clubs & spaces
cells.value: The four inquiry rooms — Geography, Srijan, Model UN and Active Learning.

close.heading:
Four of twelve,
spent on the {{open questions.}}
body: The school enumerates its twelve rooms and names the four inquiry rooms among them. It does not publish club membership, meeting times or who runs each one — and it has published no photograph of the Robotics Lab or of the four inquiry rooms in use.
